paper.title: Pure Exploration in Kernel and Neural Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit pure exploration with adaptive embedding (misspecified linear embeddings)
unmapped: reward h: X -> [-1,1] is arbitrary; for every d a known feature map psi_d with h = <psi_d(x), theta_d> + eta_d(x), |eta_d| <= tilde_gamma(d)
the learner knows the feature maps psi_d and the misspecification function tilde_gamma(.)
gamma(d) assumed to go to 0 as d grows
settings.definition_quote: Consider a set of arms $\cX \subseteq \R^D$ ... unknown function $h: \cX \rightarrow [-1,1]$ ... noise $\xi$ is assumed to be $1$-sub-Gaussian ... For any $d \in \N$, we assume the existence of a feature mapping $\bpsi_d: \cX \rightarrow \R^d$ and a unknown reward vector $\btheta_d$ such that $h(\bx) = \ang*{\bpsi_d(\bx), \btheta_d} + \eta_d(\bx)$ ... We assume the knowledge of both the feature mapping $\bpsi_d(\cdot)$ and the error function $\widetilde \gamma (\cdot)$.

unmapped: the learner knows the Mercer eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the kernel
Mercer kernel on a compact set with polynomial or exponential eigenvalue decay (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a kernel function $\cK: \cZ \times \cZ \rightarrow \R$ over a compact set $\cZ$ ... We assume $\cX \subseteq \cZ$ and the true reward of any arm $\bx \in \cX$ is given by an unknown function $h \in \cH$ such that $\norm{h}_{\cH} \leq 1$. ... We assume the knowledge of eigenfunctions and eigenvalues in this paper.

unmapped: finite arm set of unit-norm vectors with NTK gram matrix H >= lambda_0 I (Assumption 2)
S >= sqrt(h^T H^-1 h) used to tune the algorithm
settings.definition_quote: At the core of our algorithm is to use a neural network $f(\xb; \btheta)$ to learn the unknown reward function $h$ ... There exists $\lambda_0>0$ such that $\Hb \succeq \lambda_0 \Ib$. For any $\xb \in \cX$, the arm $\xb$ satisfies $\|\xb\|_2 = 1$ ...

algorithms.name: Arm Elimination with Adaptive Embedding and Induced Misspecification (Algorithm 1; KernelEmbedding / LinearEmbedding)
Arm Elimination with Fixed Embedding and Induced Misspecification (Algorithm 3)
Arm Elimination with Fixed Embedding and Unknown Misspecification (Algorithm 4)

symbols.d_eff_eps: effective dimension d_eff(epsilon) = min{d >= 1 : gamma(d) <= epsilon}

conditions: known feature maps and misspecification levels

source.label: thm:active_elim_adaptive
source.quote: With probability of at least $1-\delta$, \cref{alg:active_elim_adaptive} correctly outputs an $\epsilon$-optimal arm with sample complexity upper bounded by 640 \sum_{k=1}^{\ceil*{\log_2(2/\epsilon)}} ( ( k \, \rho_{d_k}^\star(2^{2-k}) \log(k^2 \abs{\cX}^2/\delta)) + (r_{d_k}(\zeta)+1) )= \widetilde{O} ( d_{\eff}(\epsilon) \cdot \max \{\Delta_{\min}, \epsilon\}^{-2} )

results.notes: Only the Õ form is recorded; the exact instance-dependent sum over rounds with rho*_{d_k}(2^{2-k}) is in the theorem. The canonical d_eff symbol has a different (kernel) meaning, so a new symbol is declared.

symbols.rho_d: rho*_d(gamma(d)), instance complexity of the design problem in the d-dim embedding
symbols.gamma_d: gamma(d) = (16 + 8 sqrt(g(d,zeta))) tilde_gamma(d), the accuracy achieved
symbols.r_d: r_d(zeta), number of samples needed for rounding in R^d

source.label: thm:active_elim
source.quote: With probability of at least $1-\delta$, \cref{alg:active_elim} correctly outputs an $\gamma (d)$-optimal arm with sample complexity upper bounded by N \leq 640 \, \rho_d^\star(\gamma(d)) \log_2 (\frac{4}{ \gamma(d)}) \log ( \frac{\log_2 (4/ \gamma(d)) \abs{\cX}^2 }{\delta} ) + (r_d(\zeta) + 1) \log_2 (\frac{4}{ \gamma(d)}).

results.notes: Appendix result for the fixed-embedding variant.

symbols.rho_bar: rho*(bar_gamma(d)), instance complexity at accuracy bar_gamma(d)
symbols.n_d: n(d), critical number of iterations where misspecification remains controlled

conditions: misspecification level tilde_gamma(d) unknown to the learner
guarantee is unverifiable: algorithm starts outputting a bar_gamma(d)-optimal arm after N samples but does not stop

source.label: thm:active_elim_unknown
source.quote: Suppose $\widetilde \gamma(d)$ is unknown. With probability of at least $1-\delta$, \cref{alg:active_elim_unknown} starts to output a $\overline \gamma(d)$-optimal arm after at most $N$ samples where N \leq 640 \, \rho^\star(\overline \gamma(d)) \log_2 (n(d)) \log ( \frac{(n(d) \abs{\cX})^2 }{\delta} ) + (r(\zeta) + 1) \, n(d).

results.notes: Unverifiable sample complexity; learner does not know tilde_gamma here though setting s1 lists it as known (recorded in conditions).

symbols.beta_k: eigenvalue decay exponent of the kernel (mu_j <= C_k j^-beta)

conditions: kernel has (C_k, beta)-polynomial eigenvalue decay with beta > 3/2

source.label: thm:kernel_elim
source.quote: Suppose $\cK$ has $(C_k, \beta)$-polynomial eigenvalue decay. We have $d_{\eff}(\epsilon) = O ({\epsilon}^{-2/(2\beta -3)})$, and the sample complexity of identifying an $\epsilon$-optimal arm is upper bounded by $\widetilde O ( \epsilon^{-2/(2\beta -3)} \max \{\Delta_{\min}, \epsilon\}^{-2} )$.

results.notes: Holds with probability >= 1-delta via Theorem thm:active_elim_adaptive.

conditions: kernel has (C_k, beta)-exponential eigenvalue decay with beta > 0

source.label: thm:kernel_elim
source.quote: Suppose $\cK$ has $(C_k, \beta)$-exponential eigenvalue decay. We have $d_{\eff}(\epsilon) = O (\log(1/\epsilon))$, and the sample complexity of identifying an $\epsilon$-optimal arm is upper bounded by $\widetilde O (\max \{\Delta_{\min}, \epsilon\}^{-2})$.

symbols.d_eff_neural: neural effective dimension d_eff(bar_eps^2/|X|) = min{d : sum_{i>d} lambda_i(H) <= bar_eps^2/|X|}

conditions: Assumption 2: H >= lambda_0 I, ||x||_2 = 1, symmetric coordinates, symmetric initialization
network width m = poly(|X|, L, 1/lambda_0, log(|X|/delta_k), N_k, alpha, 1/bar_eps)
tuning: eta_k = C_1 (m alpha + N_k m L)^-1
J_k = log(C_2 eps^2 alpha/(N_k L))/(eta_k m L)

source.label: thm:neural
source.quote: then when $m = \text{poly}(|\cX|, L, \lambda_0^{-1}, \log(|\cX|/\delta_k), N_k, \alpha, \bar \epsilon^{-1})$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\widehat{\cS}_{n+1}$ only includes arm $\xb$ satisfying $\Delta_{\xb} \leq \epsilon$, and the total sample complexity of Algorithm \ref{alg:neural} is bounded by N = \widetilde O((1+\zeta)d_{\eff}(\bar \epsilon^2/|\cX|)/\epsilon^2 + r_{d_{\eff}(\bar \epsilon^2/|\cX|)}(\zeta) ) = \widetilde O(d_{\eff}(\bar \epsilon^2/|\cX|) \epsilon^{-2}).

results.notes: Formal version of informal Theorem 1 (thm:neural_inf); recorded once. Guarantee is that all surviving arms are epsilon-optimal.
